intro: Japanese treats ability less as an action you perform and more as a state that holds of something: Japanese is speakable for me, the sea is visible. So the thing you can do, see or understand is marked が, like the subject of a state, and the person who can is the topic (は), or に for できる and わかる.

skills.rule: What you can do, see or understand takes が; with できる, わかる, 見える and 聞こえる it is never を, while other potential verbs (話せる, 食べられる) also accept を.
skills.explain:
できる, わかる, 見える and 聞こえる never take を: 日本語がわかります, ピアノができます, 富士山が見えます, 音楽が聞こえます. These are the ones that catch English speakers, because "understand", "play" and "see" take an object in English.

Potential forms of ordinary verbs (話す → 話せる, 食べる → 食べられる, 読む → 読める) take が as the textbook choice: 中国語が話せます. を is also correct and common in speech, especially when the object is long or far from the verb: 一人で着物を着られる. In the drill, が is always right for these.

The person who can is は: 田中さんは中国語が話せます. In negatives and contrasts the object often switches to は: 漢字は読めますが、書けません. Inside a noun-modifying clause が can become の: 日本語の話せる人. 見られる and 聞ける are deliberate (can go and see); 見える and 聞こえる are things reaching your senses by themselves.
patterns: [thing] が [できる / わかる / 見える / 聞こえる]
[verb dictionary form] こと が できる

examples.jp: 私[わたし]はピアノ{が}できます。
田中[たなか]さんは中国語[ちゅうごくご]{が}話[はな]せます。
窓[まど]から海[うみ]{が}見[み]えます。
examples.en: You can see the sea from the window.

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]の答[こた]え{が}わかりません。
examples.en: I don't know the answer to this question.

examples.jp: 辛[から]い物[もの]{が}食[た]べられますか。
隣[となり]の部屋[へや]から音楽[おんがく]{が}聞[き]こえます。
examples.en: I can hear music from the next room.

contrast.note: は marks the person who can (田中さんは), or the object when you contrast or deny (漢字は読めますが…). For a plain statement of what you can do, the thing is が.
に can mark the person with できる and わかる (私にはできない "it's beyond me"), never the thing you can do.
の replaces が only inside a clause that modifies a noun: 日本語の話せる人. At the end of a sentence 日本語の話せます is wrong.

mistakes.bad: 日本語[にほんご]をわかります。
mistakes.good: 日本語[にほんご]{が}わかります。
mistakes.note: わかる never takes を. What you understand is が.

mistakes.bad: ここから富士山[ふじさん]を見[み]えます。
mistakes.good: ここから富士山[ふじさん]{が}見[み]えます。
mistakes.note: 見える means "is visible". The thing seen is が, never を.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]はピアノをできます。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]はピアノ{が}できます。
mistakes.note: できる takes が for the skill. を is wrong with できる.

skills.tip: Rephrase "I can X" as "X is possible for me". X is the subject of a state, so X gets が.
